title: The Waterlily's Invitation
story:
James stood at the edge of the cobblestone towpath, mesmerized by the rise and fall of the green water. He had seen the Great Canopy's wild, rushing rivers. He had seen the oily, dark puddles of the Oakhaven border. He had never seen water so perfectly tamed, held in place by cool gray stone and moving with the slow, deliberate breath of the town.

A low, rhythmic chugging broke his trance. Rounding the bend came a long, flat-bottomed wooden barge, its dark wood polished by years of river-mist. On its bow, painted in faded cream letters, was the name The Waterlily. Steering the craft from the stern was a man with a beard like river-foam, wearing a heavy blue woolen vest. This was Silas, a quiet boatman who spent his days hauling crates of apples and flour between Oakhaven's districts.

Silas did not shout or wave. He simply slowed the barge to a gentle drift, his eyes meeting James's with a soft, knowing crinkle. Reaching into his deep pocket, Silas pulled out a small, smooth piece of green sea-glass, worn perfectly round by the tide. He tossed it gently onto the towpath. It landed with a soft clack near James's feet. Silas nodded toward an empty wooden crate on the deck of his barge, a silent invitation to climb aboard.

James hesitated, his fingers brushing against the brass map canister at his side. But the canal water hummed a song of quiet journeys, and the barge looked sturdy and safe. With a nimble leap, James caught the smooth wooden rail, pulled himself up, and pocketed the green sea-glass. As the barge drifted away from the library steps, Oakhaven began to reveal itself from a whole new angle, slipping slowly past him like an unfolding scroll.

The air beneath the stone bridges was cool and smelled of damp earth and old iron. James sat atop a wooden crate, holding his knees, watching the reflections of Oakhaven's tall brick chimneys dance upside down in the ripples. Ahead, the canal stretched into a tunnel of weeping willows, where the morning sun filtered through the leaves in long, golden shafts.
location: Oakhaven, aboard The Waterlily canal barge
